youtubeTitle: The Gospel and Soul Health Session 37 - Dr Bruce Wauchope
topic: Gospel recap: Christ in our darkness; the dodgy gospel
summary: Opening the chapter on the conscience, Bruce recaps the gospel using volunteers: Father, Son and Spirit love one another, are one (Deuteronomy 6:4), and purpose to catch humanity up in their love. God is love, not love here and justice there, which is pagan Greek thinking; God's wrath arises when this purpose is violated. Christ gives Zoe life to all, and darkness is not absence of light but life lived without love. The Word alone became human, entering not just a body but our flesh, our darkness, and because he holds all things together, what happened to him happened to us: deicide was suicide, and Father and Spirit never took a holiday. Christ is now in each person's black hole, and the veil being pulled back is his coming. Bruce recaps the healing overview and ends by naming the 'dodgy gospel' (Dan Dorman's term), based on Greek philosophy and a chasm of separation, which feeds the flesh and locks us in fear and guilt.
keyPoints: Father, Son and Spirit love one another and are so much in each other that they are one; that oneness is not singular but tri-personal (Deuteronomy 6:4; Psalms 2 and 110).
The pre-creation purpose is that humanity be caught up in their love; if you don't start with these scriptures you end in the wrong spot.
God is love; 'love over here and justice over there' is pagan Greek philosophy. God is wrathful when the purpose of love is being violated.
The universe is held within Christ like a womb (Colossians 1:16-17), and his Zoe life flows through everyone; our lives are not self-sustained.
Darkness is not the absence of light but failing to see it; it is life lived without love, which is how Hitler, Stalin, Pol Pot, and we ourselves create death.
Only the Word became human, even an embryo, so only he can reveal the Father; he took not just anthropos (human body) but sarx (our flesh, our darkness) (John 1:14).
Jesus' body had as much flesh as anyone in history; he overcame God-out-there, the accuser, internal contradictions and deep pain (Hebrews 10:5).
Because he holds all together, what we did to him we did to ourselves: deicide was suicide; if one died for all, all died (2 Corinthians 5:14); he went into Hades to free those trapped there.
Father and Spirit don't take a holiday at the incarnation or cross; the Trinity is indivisible.
Christ is now in every person's flesh, including the black hole; the second coming is the veil being pulled back so humanity sees Christ in us.

Healing recap: forgiveness shuts down the judge, guilt and fear unlock, defences and the stairway fall, mess returns, pain management and spin ease, parts return, and we drop through the black hole to find ourselves held by Dad.

The 'dodgy gospel' (Dan Dorman's term) posits an abyss between God and humanity and misquotes Habakkuk 1:13; it feeds the flesh, leaving us to construct our own way back and locking us in fear and guilt.

keyTerms.definition: Father, Son and Spirit so in each other that they are one God, a tri-personal unity rather than a singular one.
The life of Christ flowing through all creation.
Not the absence of light but life lived without seeing or knowing love.
Christ took both a human body (anthropos) and our fallen flesh or darkness (sarx).
Because Christ holds humanity together, in killing him we died with him.
The veil pulled back so humanity sees Christ already in us.
The Greek-influenced Western gospel of separation and an abyss, which feeds the flesh rather than bringing life and love.

quotes: It's not love over here and justice over there; that's thoroughly pagan.
If I live the flow of life in darkness, without love, I'm in darkness.
Everything of Father, Son and Spirit leads to integration and oneness.

caseStudy.title: A God who can't look at me
caseStudy.scenario: Chris was taught that God is holy and cannot look upon sin, so after any failure he feels God turn away. He works hard to 'get back' through extra prayer and service, but feels anxious and exhausted. His relationships suffer because he is always measuring himself and others.
caseStudy.analysis: Chris is living inside the dodgy gospel: an abyss of separation and a God whose justice competes with his love. Bruce argues this feeds the flesh, locking Chris in fear and guilt and making him construct his own way back. The undiluted gospel says Christ already holds him and has entered his darkness.
pathway: Read Colossians 1:16-17 and notice there is nowhere outside Christ.
Re-examine the 'God can't look on sin' idea in light of Jesus eating with sinners.
Notice the anxiety and striving as symptoms of a separation story, not truth.
Practise resting rather than performing after a failure: 'Christ is in me here.'
Talk with a mentor or counsellor about the fear and exhaustion.

practices.name: Light or darkness check
practices.how: Choose one activity today (work, a conversation) and ask: 'Am I living this flow of life in love?' Adjust one small thing toward love.

practices.name: Trinity contemplation
practices.how: Spend five minutes picturing the Father, Son and Spirit loving one another, with you caught up in the middle.

practices.name: Rewrite the story
practices.how: Write the gospel you were taught in three sentences, then rewrite it in three sentences of union, and compare how each makes you feel.

reflection: Have you thought of God's love and justice as competing? How does Bruce's view change that?
What would it mean that Christ is present in your black hole right now?
In what ways has a gospel of separation shaped how you treat yourself and others?
